pairs.subject: test-input-generation
pairs.evidence: lib/foundry/scout/seeds.ts:124 The seed door is a fail-first accept-or-reject gate whose reason is the caller's instruction for what to fix, yet nothing checks that reason against a model of the rules each input breaks; its tests break one rule per hand-written case, so a wrong rule reported when two are broken, or a precedence defect, cannot be seen.

techniques.evidence: lib/foundry/scout/museDoor.ts:122 The muse door also returns the first rule it hits. Its tests (scout-muse-idea.test.ts:155-187) pin one recorded reason per input that breaks one rule. The technique says that kind of suite can never see a wrong-rule or precedence defect. A model that predicts the set of broken rules, run over combinations, is missing.

tests/next-server/scout-seeds.test.ts:95 Invalid inputs are valid briefs with one field pushed just past its limit (SEED_SENTENCE_MAX is 200, MAX_SEED_BATCH + 1, age 24 against a minimum of 25, 51 against a maximum of 50). Each test asserts the specific reason, and line 104 asserts nothing was written.

tests/next-server/scout-seeds.test.ts:93 Inputs are built by hand-written helpers like brief(). There is no randomized generator whose reach could be bounded; no fast-check, Math.random or fuzz turned up in lib/foundry/scout.
